function.mechanism: In aqueous food systems, glucono-delta-lactone hydrolyzes gradually to gluconic acid, causing controlled acidification and pH reduction.

adi.basis: No accessible EFSA final E575 re-evaluation with a numerical ADI was retrieved in this run; checked EFSA call URLs were unavailable (404/page-not-found) on 2026-02-27.

efsa.key_finding: E575 is present in EU additive legislation (Union list/specifications), but no retrievable final EFSA E575 re-evaluation output was identified from accessible EFSA pages in this run.

fda.notes: Affirmed as GRAS direct human food ingredient; used with no limitation other than current good manufacturing practice; functions include curing/pickling, leavening, pH control, and sequestration.

adi.basis: ADI NOT SPECIFIED (group ADI including glucono-delta-lactone and selected gluconate salts).

concerns.summary: A 21-day young-rat high-dose study with additive combinations (including gluconolactone) reported neurobehavioral and neurotransmitter changes, strongest in combination/high-dose groups.
Modern oral-human long-term safety data specific to E575 as a standalone food additive are limited in the retrieved literature.

no_concern_confirmed: FDA affirms glucono-delta-lactone as GRAS for direct human food use under GMP conditions (21 CFR 184.1318).
JECFA lists ADI as not specified for a group including glucono-delta-lactone.
EU legislation continues to list E575 in additive and specification texts reviewed.

adi_exceedance.notes: No numerical ADI is set by JECFA for this group additive context; an EFSA numerical ADI for E575 was not identified in accessible EFSA pages in this run.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory evidence indicates low concern at authorized/GMP use levels (FDA GRAS and JECFA ADI not specified), with no identified IARC classification or major bans. However, modern additive-specific oral safety evidence in humans is limited and a retrievable final EFSA E575 re-evaluation was not identified in the checked EFSA pages.
